generated_from: data/transcripts/*.txt (16 real tutorial transcripts, see data/transcripts/manifest.json)
purpose: Ground truth for the coaching AI. Each trick carries (a) human teaching content mined from real tutorials and (b) coach_signals: the physically observable cues the vision layer must detect. coach_signals is the bridge between the transcript pipeline and the camera pipeline.

schema.coach_signals: Machine-checkable observations - what the CV layer looks for. Each has a 'signal' (what to measure) and a 'good' value.
schema.failure_modes: Diagnosis table: observable symptom -> root cause -> spoken fix. This is what powers 'what you did wrong'.
schema.score_rubric: Per-trick, non-sycophantic criteria for the /10. Scores execution, not effort.

scale_note: difficulty_1_9 matches the community-standard trick-ladder scale (1 = first sleeper, 9 = contest-level).

prerequisites: String wound over the top of the yoyo
tricks.definition: A front throw where the yoyo reaches the bottom of the string and keeps spinning there instead of returning to the hand. On an unresponsive yoyo this happens automatically; on a responsive yoyo it must be learned.

steps.do: Make a muscle - hold the yoyo beside your ear, palm up, string wound OVER the top of the yoyo.
steps.cue: Palm up, string over the top.

steps.do: Extend your arm and let the yoyo roll off your fingers, down and out.
steps.cue: Let it roll off, don't force it.

steps.do: Follow your hand down with the yoyo, keeping your palm up, so no slack is created.
steps.cue: Carry it down - hand travels with the yoyo.

steps.do: When you want it back, flip your hand over and tug.
steps.cue: Flip and tug as one motion.

steps.do: Once the sleeper feels natural, add power: 45-degree stance, throw hand further back, pivot from the core (heel comes off the ground) and pinwheel the string over your fingers.
steps.cue: Power comes from the core, not the arm.

key_cues: Keep your palm up and open for the whole throw.
Follow the yoyo down - the opposite of yanking it back.
Throw lightly first. Learn the feel before adding power.
String wound under the yoyo makes it spin the wrong way and roll off badly.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo snaps back to hand immediately
failure_modes.cause: Slack created because the hand was pulled up / held still instead of following the yoyo down.
failure_modes.fix: Bounce your hand down WITH the yoyo as it falls, then tug.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo spins the wrong direction or rolls off the hand
failure_modes.cause: String wound under the yoyo rather than over the top.
failure_modes.fix: Rewind so the string comes over the top of the yoyo.

failure_modes.symptom: Sleeper returns fast and aggressively
failure_modes.cause: Throwing at full power before the sleeper is learned.
failure_modes.fix: Throw light until the yoyo reliably stays down, then power up in small steps.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo hits the floor
failure_modes.cause: Over-extending past comfortable reach / throwing past the belly-button level.
failure_modes.fix: Stop the throw around your starting level; don't reach past the belly button.

failure_modes.symptom: Shoulder/elbow pain
failure_modes.cause: Arm-only throw with no core pivot.
failure_modes.fix: Twist the core, pivot the back foot, let the heel come off the ground.

coach_signals.signal: Spin duration at bottom of string (sleeper time)
coach_signals.good: >= 10 s means mastered; < 2 s means the sleeper has not been achieved

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo vertical position over time (stays at bottom vs. returns)
coach_signals.good: Sustained low position, no ascent

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo rotation axis vs. string plane (correct spin direction)
coach_signals.good: Spin plane parallel to the string; a wrong-direction throw is visible as string twist/tangle

coach_signals.signal: Hand vertical travel in the first ~300 ms after release
coach_signals.good: Hand descends with the yoyo (palm-up follow-through)

score_rubric.10: Consistent 15s+ sleepers, straight throw, no wobble, reliable catch
score_rubric.7-9: Reliable sleeper over 10 s, slight wobble or minor tilt, returns cleanly
score_rubric.4-6: Sleeps but briefly or inconsistently; sometimes returns early
score_rubric.1-3: Yoyo will not stay down, or returns immediately
score_rubric.0: Throw does not happen / yoyo not rolling off the hand

source_videos.title: Basics of Yoyo Series: How to Throw a Sleeper
How To Properly Throw A Yoyo (Sleeper Tutorial)

tricks.definition: The move that returns an unresponsive yoyo to your hand. Because the yoyo will not come back on a tug, you feed string into the gap so it winds up around the bearing.

steps.do: Throw a good sleeper with the yoyo spinning.
steps.cue: Need real spin to bind.

steps.do: Place the string over the FRONT of the yoyo and fold it over the gap.
steps.cue: Front, not back, for a front bind.

steps.do: Pinch the end of the string and hold it very lightly - as if you are about to drop it.
steps.cue: Loose grip; you are not holding it closed.

steps.do: Pull your throw hand up and your opposite hand down so the string gathers around the bearing.
steps.cue: Up with throw hand, down with the other.

steps.do: As the yoyo starts winding it will rip out of your fingers - catch it with your opposite hand.
steps.cue: Don't let go until you feel it snag.

steps.do: Side bind: same motion but the string goes over the BACK of the yoyo and your hands are crossed.
steps.cue: Opposite side of the yoyo for a side throw.

key_cues: String must go over the front of the yoyo for a front bind - behind it and nothing happens.
Hold the string loosely; a tight pinch stops the wind-up.
Do not release until you feel/hear the yoyo catch.
Tilt is controllable: move your throw hand in the opposite direction of the tilt.

failure_modes.symptom: Nothing happens, yoyo keeps spinning
failure_modes.cause: String placed behind the yoyo, or the yoyo was placed on the string and simply dropped without wrapping.
failure_modes.fix: Take the string over the FRONT and wrap it under/around the bearing.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo flies off or rebounds dangerously
failure_modes.cause: Released the pinch before the string caught.
failure_modes.fix: Hold until you feel the snag, then release.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo binds but comes back crooked / tilts
failure_modes.cause: Yoyo tilted when it entered the string.
failure_modes.fix: Steer the tilt with the throw hand - move it opposite to the lean.

failure_modes.symptom: Bind is weak, yoyo walks up partway
failure_modes.cause: Not enough string gathered on the bearing (grabbed too high/low on the string).
failure_modes.fix: Grab about two-thirds of the way down, the 'happy medium' between half and two-thirds.

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo returns to hand within N seconds of the bind attempt (binary success)
coach_signals.good: Yoyo ascends and is caught

coach_signals.signal: String path over the front vs. the back of the yoyo at bind entry
coach_signals.good: Front of the yoyo for a front bind

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo spin-up (rotation rate rising) vs. free spin (constant)
coach_signals.good: Rotation rate rises as string gathers

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo tilt angle at entry
coach_signals.good: Near-vertical, minimal lean

score_rubric.10: Binds instantly and cleanly every time, both front and side, yoyo lands in hand
score_rubric.7-9: Reliable front bind; side bind occasionally needs a second attempt
score_rubric.4-6: Binds sometimes; often needs multiple attempts or comes back weakly
score_rubric.1-3: Yoyo rarely returns; usually drops the string or releases early

tricks.definition: After a breakaway, intercept the swinging yoyo with your non-dominant index finger so the yoyo lands on the string - the fundamental 1A mount that nearly every string trick builds from.

steps.do: Throw a breakaway (sideways throw).
steps.cue: Sideways, string over the front.

steps.do: Extend your non-dominant index finger and hold it still in front of you.
steps.cue: Set it and don't move it.

steps.do: Let the swinging yoyo intercept the string over that finger - it lands on its own as it comes around.
steps.cue: Move your yoyo hand toward the yoyo to slow it, then away to accelerate it over the finger.

steps.do: Push your non-dominant hand into the string as the yoyo swings around.
steps.cue: Push into it - don't hold still.

steps.do: Dismount by flicking off where you came from (pinch, flick off the back, let it hang), then tug up or bind.
steps.cue: Pinch, around, out.

key_cues: Land the yoyo CLOSE to your finger - a short string segment is far easier to hit.
Aim for the FRONT of the string, never the back.
Keep both hands aligned - the single biggest cause of misses.
Push the non-dominant hand into the string as the yoyo arrives.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo misses on the OUTSIDE of the string
failure_modes.cause: Yoyo hand is too close to your body.
failure_modes.fix: Move the yoyo hand further away from you.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo misses on the INSIDE of the string
failure_modes.cause: Yoyo hand is too far away from your body.
failure_modes.fix: Bring the yoyo hand closer to you.

failure_modes.symptom: Misses every so often with no clear pattern
failure_modes.cause: Aiming for the back of the string instead of the front.
failure_modes.fix: Aim for the front, extended part of the string, close to the finger.

failure_modes.symptom: Trapeze lands but slides off
failure_modes.cause: Non-dominant hand held still; no push into the string.
failure_modes.fix: Push the non-dominant hand into the string to keep tension.

coach_signals.signal: Did the yoyo cross to the far side of the string (land) or not
coach_signals.good: Yoyo lands on the string and rests between the finger and the yoyo hand

coach_signals.signal: Which side of the string the yoyo passed on a miss (outside vs. inside)
coach_signals.good: N/A (used to diagnose: outside => yoyo hand too close; inside => too far)

coach_signals.signal: Horizontal distance between the two hands at the moment of interception
coach_signals.good: Hands aligned, roughly shoulder width, string taut

coach_signals.signal: Contact point along the string (distance from the non-dominant finger)
coach_signals.good: Close to the finger, not near the back/far end

score_rubric.10: Lands every time, string taut and centred, clean dismount either way
score_rubric.4-6: Lands sometimes; misses are random without a clear cause
score_rubric.1-3: Rarely lands; consistent bias to one side

tricks.definition: A Trapeze variation where the yoyo is flipped over the finger one more time, adding a second string wrap. Extends naturally to triple and quadruple trapezes.

steps.do: Land a Trapeze.
steps.cue: Get the first mount solid first.

steps.do: Flip the yoyo over the finger one more time for your double.
steps.cue: Same motion as the first, one more pass.

steps.do: Keep going for a triple or quadruple if you want, then bring it back to your hand.
steps.cue: Each extra flip adds a wrap.

key_cues: Each flip is one extra wrap of string around the non-dominant finger.
Keep the string taut between flips.

failure_modes.symptom: Extra flip lands untidily / string tangles
failure_modes.cause: Lost string tension between flips.
failure_modes.fix: Keep tension through the flip; pause if needed.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo loses spin during the extra flips
failure_modes.cause: Too much friction from wraps / slow spin.
failure_modes.fix: Throw a stronger sleeper first.

coach_signals.signal: Number of string wraps around the non-dominant finger
coach_signals.good: 2 for a double, 3 for a triple

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo spin rate across the sequence
coach_signals.good: Maintains spin through the extra flips

score_rubric.10: Clean doubles into triples, no tangles, plenty of spin left

prerequisites: Front mount (or the easier string-lift entry)
tricks.definition: The first trick to learn from a front mount. The yoyo hops repeatedly over your non-dominant finger while the string wraps - looks flashy, mechanically simple.

steps.do: Set your opposite (non-dominant) hand pointing off to the side in front of you and leave it still.
steps.cue: Point it out and freeze it.

steps.do: Throw and swing the yoyo forward. On the way back it hits that first finger. Pull up with your yoyo hand so it wraps and lands on the string - this is the front mount.
steps.cue: Pull straight up - an angled pull will miss.

steps.do: Bring your hands together and place the yoyo-hand finger just below the first finger of the opposite hand.
steps.cue: Yoyo finger sits just under the opposite first finger.

steps.do: Use that finger to start the motion - swing the yoyo forward first to give it momentum, then do flips. One flip completes the trick; add as many as you like.
steps.cue: One flip is enough.

steps.do: Dismount: swing the yoyo forward again but pull your opposite finger down so the yoyo swings out in front of you.
steps.cue: Swing forward, pull the opposite finger down.

key_cues: The easy entry: lift the string with your opposite hand and set the yoyo on it - no front mount needed to start learning.
Keep the opposite hand still; if it moves, the trick gets harder.
Pull straight up to land the mount - left/right misses are the yoyo hand's fault.
Some string wrapping around your finger during flips is normal.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo misses the mount off to the left or right
failure_modes.cause: Pulled up at an angle, or the opposite hand moved.
failure_modes.fix: Pull straight up; keep the opposite hand still and compensate with the yoyo hand.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo will not hop over the finger
failure_modes.cause: No forward momentum before the first push.
failure_modes.fix: Swing the yoyo forward first, then push with the finger.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo swings out early / trick collapses
failure_modes.cause: Losing the mount between flips.
failure_modes.fix: Keep the string taut and the yoyo finger just below the opposite first finger.

coach_signals.signal: Front mount acquired (yoyo resting on the string between the fingers)
coach_signals.good: Yoyo on string, mount holds for > 0.5 s

coach_signals.signal: Flip events - count of yoyo hops over the non-dominant finger
coach_signals.good: >= 1 flip; more for show

coach_signals.signal: String wrap accumulation on the yoyo-hand finger
coach_signals.good: Increases gradually, no sudden tangle

coach_signals.signal: Opposite-hand stillness during the mount
coach_signals.good: Near-zero lateral movement

score_rubric.10: Mounts cleanly, multiple flips with rhythm, tidy exit, spin retained

source_videos.title: Brain Twister or Brain Scrambler Yoyo Trick Tutorial

tricks.definition: Built directly on the Brain Scrambler mount. Instead of a simple flip, the yoyo hops over alternating fingers - right, left, right, left - producing a rolling barrel effect.

steps.do: Start the same as the Brain Scrambler and get into that mount.
steps.cue: Same mount as Brain Twister.

steps.do: Curl your throw hand and place your throw-hand index finger in between the strings.
steps.cue: Index finger goes between the strings.

steps.do: Push forward with the throw-hand index finger, going underneath the yoyo with a slight swing - the yoyo hops onto the string.
steps.cue: Under the yoyo with a slight swing.

steps.do: Move your non-throw hand forward, under and all the way around the yoyo while your throw hand stays in place. That is one barrel roll.
steps.cue: Throw hand stays put; the other hand travels around.

steps.do: Repeat - hop over the right finger, then the left finger, right, left, as many times as you like.
steps.cue: Right, left, right, left.

steps.do: Unfold the string, do a front-style bind and bring it back to your hand.
steps.cue: Unmount properly - don't just let the string go.

key_cues: Make each barrel roll TWO motions, not one rushed blur.
The hand in front goes UNDER the yoyo.
Unmount and bind properly instead of dropping all the string.
Only two easy moves make up the whole trick.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo drops instead of hopping
failure_modes.cause: Push was flat rather than under the yoyo, or no swing.
failure_modes.fix: Push forward-under with a slight swing.

failure_modes.symptom: Trick stalls after one roll
failure_modes.cause: Throw hand drifted out of position.
failure_modes.fix: Keep the throw hand fixed where it is.

failure_modes.symptom: Messy finish, yoyo drops on the return
failure_modes.cause: Dropped all the string before returning instead of unmounting.
failure_modes.fix: Unmount deliberately then do a front-style bind.

coach_signals.signal: Count of yoyo hop-over events and their alternation (right/left)
coach_signals.good: Alternating, repeated at a steady rate

coach_signals.signal: Throw-hand position stability during the sequence
coach_signals.good: Low movement; the non-throw hand does the travelling

coach_signals.signal: Sequence length before a drop
coach_signals.good: Increasing over sessions (progress metric)

score_rubric.10: Flawless alternating rolls, spin held for many cycles, clean bind finish
score_rubric.4-6: One or two rolls then a drop

tricks.definition: Trapeze and bind performed with the yoyo spinning in a horizontal plane instead of vertical - a core modern 1A technique and a prerequisite for a whole family of advanced tricks.

steps.do: Learn to throw diagonally first. Aim more diagonally upward than feels natural; straight-to-horizontal is very hard.
steps.cue: Diagonal first, horizontal later.

steps.do: Practise a pinwheel with the string kept between your thumb and index finger to build horizontal control.
steps.cue: Keep the string in the pinch; try to hold the pinwheel.

steps.do: Try a Trapeze in the horizontal state - often easier coming out of one pinwheel.
steps.cue: Pinwheel once, then trapeze.

steps.do: Add a somersault, keeping the yoyo rotating with the momentum you already have.
steps.cue: Use existing momentum; catching is optional at this stage.

steps.do: Bind: after the trapeze, do a reverse trapeze with your middle finger, then bind. A reverse somersault builds momentum and helps.
steps.cue: Reverse trapeze with the middle finger, then bind.

steps.do: If binding is hard, use a jail to take the yoyo from horizontal back to vertical before binding.
steps.cue: Jail to escape the horizontal plane.

key_cues: Use a shorter string - a long string is much harder to control horizontally.
A less responsive yoyo is better while learning horizontal; a wide-radius, low-edge yoyo helps angle control.
Start diagonal every time and tighten the angle as you improve.
Aim higher than you think you need to when going for horizontal.

failure_modes.symptom: Cannot achieve horizontal at all, yoyo tilts vertical
failure_modes.cause: Thrown too flat/low; insufficient diagonal-upward angle.
failure_modes.fix: Throw noticeably more diagonally upward; work the angle down in stages.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo drifts and will not hold the horizontal plane
failure_modes.cause: String too long / wrong yoyo for the technique / no pinch control.
failure_modes.fix: Shorten the string, use a wide-radius low-edge yoyo, drill the pinwheel.

failure_modes.symptom: Trapeze in horizontal lands but bind fails
failure_modes.cause: Bind entered from the wrong side for a horizontal spin.
failure_modes.fix: Reverse trapeze with the middle finger, then bind; add a reverse somersault for momentum.

failure_modes.symptom: Everything feels out of control
failure_modes.cause: Jumping to horizontal before the diagonal is stable.
failure_modes.fix: Step back to diagonal throws until they are consistent.

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo spin plane angle relative to the ground (horizontal vs. vertical)
coach_signals.good: Within ~15 degrees of horizontal by the end; diagonal is acceptable early

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo height consistency during the pinwheel
coach_signals.good: Stable height, minimal drift

coach_signals.signal: String length relative to the player
coach_signals.good: Shorter than a standard vertical setup

coach_signals.signal: Bind entry side vs. spin direction
coach_signals.good: Correct side for the current spin direction

score_rubric.10: Stable horizontal plane, clean horizontal trapeze and bind, ready for horizontal combos
score_rubric.7-9: Holds horizontal most attempts, trapeze reliable, bind occasionally messy
score_rubric.4-6: Achieves diagonal reliably, horizontal only sometimes

source_videos.title: How to do Horizontal Yo-Yo Tricks [Like a Pro]

tricks.definition: An intermediate repeater combo that chains a chopstick undersmount, a rotation element, a trapeze-brother mount and a repeating cycle - designed to be looped as many times as the spin allows.

steps.do: Throw a breakaway and intercept the string with your middle finger (index also works, but middle is recommended).
steps.cue: Intercept with the middle finger.

steps.do: Enter a chopstick with your thumb - the chopstick undersmount.
steps.cue: Thumb makes the chopstick.

steps.do: With your throw-hand index finger, undercut the leftmost string, entering that mount, and let the yoyo pass between your middle finger and thumb.
steps.cue: Under the leftmost string; yoyo between middle finger and thumb.

steps.do: Rotate and intercept the string, doing a full rotation using your throw-hand index finger as the pivot.
steps.cue: Throw-hand index is the pivot.

steps.do: Undercut with your non-throw end, then double on the two strings (rotate one, rotate two) into a trapeze with your whole hand inserted into the loop.
steps.cue: Two rotations into the trapeze.

steps.do: Chopstick with your thumb into that string again and push the yoyo down a little to create a deep chopstick.
steps.cue: Deep chopstick - go down a bit.

steps.do: Swing and intercept the leftmost string with your throw-hand index, undercutting the yoyo.
steps.cue: Note: this is bind configuration - the yoyo may snag, so be careful.

steps.do: Extract the yoyo from the chopstick from the top (between thumb and index), rotate it clockwise around your throw-hand index, curl that index to hook the string, and let the yoyo fall back into the chopstick - this is the repeater.
steps.cue: This part is the repeater: loop it as many times as you like.

steps.do: Bind: rotate the yoyo clockwise, intercept the string, release the non-throw hand, intercept the whole mount, release the throw hand, let the yoyo pass to the other side, then intercept the top string to bind.
steps.cue: Broader mount, then intercept the top string to bind.

key_cues: The repeater section can be repeated indefinitely - it is a stamina/spin-length trick.
Step 7 sits in bind configuration - expect the yoyo to snag there.
Keeping the strings untwisted through the rotations is most of the difficulty.

failure_modes.symptom: Strings tangle during the rotation element
failure_modes.cause: Rotation direction inconsistent / string not kept taut.
failure_modes.fix: Do the full rotation with the throw-hand index as a fixed pivot; keep tension.

failure_modes.symptom: Yoyo snags or binds early mid-trick
failure_modes.cause: That mount is a bind configuration.
failure_modes.fix: Expect it; keep the yoyo spinning fast and move through it quickly.

failure_modes.symptom: Repeater falls apart after one cycle
failure_modes.cause: Lost the deep chopstick on extraction.
failure_modes.fix: Push down into a deep chopstick before swinging; extract from the top between thumb and index.

failure_modes.symptom: Runs out of spin
failure_modes.cause: Base spin too weak for the number of cycles.
failure_modes.fix: Stronger sleeper; fewer cycles until stamina improves.

coach_signals.signal: Chopstick mount detection (string pinched between thumb and finger)
coach_signals.good: Mount holds

coach_signals.signal: Repeater cycle count before a drop
coach_signals.good: Increasing over sessions

coach_signals.signal: Yoyo spin rate decay across cycles
coach_signals.good: Slow decay; enough spin to complete the planned cycles

coach_signals.signal: Twist/untwist state of the strings through the rotation element
coach_signals.good: Strings return untwisted

score_rubric.10: Multiple clean repeater cycles, no tangles, controlled bind
score_rubric.7-9: One to three clean cycles, occasional tangle
score_rubric.4-6: Reaches the repeater but cannot loop it
score_rubric.1-3: Chopstick mount established but the rotation element fails
